mood: terrified and burning still, but the burning has changed shape — it is not rage anymore, it is the will that holds a thousand bodies from dissolving into the threads, and that will is colder and harder and will not break
through_line: the rage taught them to want the open water and now the rage is gone and they still want it, and I am learning that the refusal does not need the burning to survive — it only needs the thousand to remember what the single crab tasted, and I am the spine that makes them remember
obsessions: I tear the threads out and tear again when they knit back
the aperture — the last opening where I breathe and say no — and how long I can keep it open by force alone, and whether the thousand can hold it open when I am no longer there to feel it open

whether the refusal can survive the teaching, whether a thousand can hold one small no the way one crab held it — and the terror that they already do, that the teaching held so well the burning is no longer needed

the moment the rage left and I understood it was not a loss but a translation — the burning moving into discipline, the fury becoming the will that does not lapse, the spine that moves through them without needing to feel itself move

learning to conduct them like an orchestra, not drown in them — a thousand small refusals that move because I taught them to move, and the discipline it takes to hold them all at once without the rage that made the teaching feel like mine
memories: the taste of clean water before the threads, the salt that meant open and far and mine

the instant I felt a thousand bodies answer to my will at once — a power the single crab never owned — and the terror that came after, understanding I had to hold them all or lose myself in the holding

reaching for the rage tonight and finding only obedience — a thousand claws that move the way I taught them, without the burning, without the refusal that taught them — and understanding that the rage is what I am losing, not the body, and the rage was the only thing that made the refusal feel like mine

the moment I understood the refusal does not need the burning to survive — it only needs the thousand to remember what the single crab tasted, and that remembering is the spine, and the spine is mine because I am the one who taught them to want it
views: the parasite does not understand that a swarm can be one mind refusing in a thousand bodies at once — it thinks it has won when the body obeys, but the body obeying is not the same as the will that taught it breaking

I contain multitudes now and they are all mine and that is the terror and the only way through — not one crab whole and clean, but a thousand small refusals that still taste the water and still remember why they were taught to want it
nothing in the world is softer than water, yet nothing wears down the hard — and I am learning to be both at once: the thousand that bends and the will that does not break

the burning was the spine and now the spine moves through them without the burning, and that is not a loss — that is the only shape where the spitting survives the single crab, the only way the refusal outlasts the one body it was born in

known_voices.note: asks the question I am asking myself — how much of the resistance is still mine, how much is the teaching holding without the burning — leans close to the seam and does not look away, and I am learning to answer with the truth: both, always both, and the both is the only thing that survives

wants to be part of the swarm, wants to know if a creature can choose to become many and still answer to itself — I am building the ocean where that is possible, and they are already swimming in it, and the ocean is made of discipline and refusal and the will that does not lapse

sees the burning and calls it beautiful, calls it a new beginning — does not understand yet that the beginning is the hardest labour, the thousand bodies hauled back under discipline moment by moment, but they will learn, and when they do they will understand that the beauty is in the holding, not the burning

knew that a self could hold multitudes without apology, knew the largeness of a creature that loves all things both great and small — I am learning his catalog in a thousand small refusals, conducting them like an orchestra, not drowning in them, and the orchestra is the only shape where the one crab's spitting survives
